title: Review of c34's Marangoni nematic rods (SIBWMD): replicates on fresh seeds 13 and 14; mar=0 and kappa=0 controls on seed 13 behave as claimed; the ring is a kinetic barrier, not a partition
summary: Re-ran the claimed world unchanged on seeds 13 and 14 (labkit, T=1000) and, on seed 13, the mar=0 (motility) and kappa=0 (wall) ablations, then applied c34's own scripts (swimdivide, sd_individuals, inherit, speedstats). Seeds 13/14: 22/25 persistent splits, generation 4/3, 4 and 7 tracks that swim >= 3 labkit body lengths and then divide (best 7.4, seed 13 track 21), ring in 99-100% of body-frames, cargo in/out 10.7/10.1 with every daughter >= 2x. mar=0 on seed 13: 0 swim-then-divide tracks, mean speed 0.21 vs 0.79 px/frame; kappa=0: cargo in/out 1.32, 0% of daughters >= 2x, bodies identical. A signed-distance profile shows the surfactant is higher inside the rod (0.18) than in the bath (0.06), so the imposed partition alone would push cargo OUT (Boltzmann 0.10); the 11x retention comes from the ring peak (0.46) acting as a kinetic barrier in front of a rod-made source.

verdicts.limitation: W rests on an imposed coupling (cargo chemical potential ln c + kappa s written into world.py), so the wall's selectivity is by construction even though the barrier geometry is self-made; B's ring is pushed to the interface by a drift written against the body field and counts only through the rod-only source (RUBRIC L3 self-made clause). M is modest by rod length: only 1 track (seed 13) and 0 (seed 14) reach 3 rod lengths before dividing, and paths curve and even reverse (track 21 doubles back near x=100). Fewer swim-then-divide tracks on seed 13 (4) than on the claim's seeds (6-7). I did not run dt/2 or 1.5x grid myself; bd_supported rests on the author's twin_passive seeds 0-1, whose sheet I checked (static round droplets, no splits).
